discovery: The theory of cosmic inflation and the quantum origin of cosmological structure
motivation: Guth proposed that a brief epoch of exponential expansion in the very early universe explains its flatness, homogeneity and the absence of relics. Linde's new and chaotic inflation made the idea workable and generic. Mukhanov, with the late Chibisov, showed that quantum vacuum fluctuations stretched during inflation seed a nearly scale-invariant spectrum of density perturbations. These predictions, including spatial flatness, adiabatic Gaussian perturbations, a slight red tilt of the spectrum and coherent acoustic peaks, have since been confirmed with great precision by COBE, WMAP, Planck and large-scale structure surveys. Inflation changed how physicists think about initial conditions. It turned quantum fluctuations into the origin of galaxies, and it links fundamental theory, including string compactifications, directly to observation. Few theoretical ideas of the past half-century have so thoroughly shaped both our picture of the cosmos and the research agenda of fundamental physics.
